purpose: HPE Aruba Networking DevHub landing, SDK, package, sample, and developer guidance pages for RAG discovery.
notes: Crawled by ingestion/scrape_devhub.py. The manifest previously pointed at scrape.py, which hardcodes the developer_docs output directory and its own seeds, so it never produced a DevHub corpus. DevHub publishes no sitemap, so pages are found by breadth-first crawl; content is in #content and query strings are dropped because the catalog filters re-render the same page. Do not commit scraped content; source URLs are preserved in each file.

purpose: New Central developer and API how-to pages from the Aruba developer portal.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape.py and scrape_cnac_spec.py, then rebuild data/docs.lance and data/specs.sqlite.

purpose: General HPE Aruba technical documentation used by docs RAG retrieval.
notes: Keep generated markdown or HTML under the git-ignored source folder with source URL comments. The doc-portal landing page is a JS doc-browser that exposes no usable book index, and only VSG serves a sitemap.xml, so the WebHelp books are walked breadth-first per book by ingestion/scrape_techdocs_books.py: CLI-Bank (the AOS-10/CoP/ClearPass/SD-Branch CLI command reference), central-on-premises, AOS-Switch-RN and AirWave. hpe-central is handled separately by ingestion/scrape_hpe_central_pw.py under the techdocs_html source. The four books above are the complete set of live WebHelp books: every ArubaDocPortal product category page (including its client-side ?tab=N panes) was enumerated and the only other in-site book root it reaches is /techdocs/Archived/, which holds superseded product versions and is deliberately excluded. /techdocs/new-central/ is only an alias that redirects into hpe-central.

purpose: Network access control, MAC registration, visitor, MPSK, DPP, and certificate reference material.
notes: Slugs discovered from the public new-central-config reference index, filtered to the NAC/AAA/security surface (261 pages), then the <article> prose is extracted with pandoc (icons/scripts stripped) at a 1.5s per-request delay. Replaces ingestion/scrape_reference.py, which read a URL list from /tmp files that no longer exist and wrote to ingestion/markdown/ instead of this output_dir — so nac_docs was silently never populated. Pair prose refreshes with the CNAC OpenAPI extraction when NAC API pages change.

purpose: Validated Solution Guide pages and design guidance used by architecture and workflow RAG answers.
notes: Build the URL list with ingestion/discover_vsg_urls.py (reads the guide's sitemap), then refresh with ingestion/scrape_vsg.py. Do not seed from /techdocs/VSG/docs/: Apache returns 403 for that directory listing even though the pages under it serve normally. Requires Playwright with headless=False for Akamai, plus pandoc for HTML->markdown. Japanese translations are excluded by default.

purpose: HPE Aruba Networking Central product documentation, feature pages, workflows, and UI terminology.
notes: The techdocs book moved from new-central to hpe-central and is now published as Oxygen WebHelp (GUID-*.html topics). Akamai 403s direct sub-resource requests, so ingestion/scrape_hpe_central_pw.py BFS-crawls topic pages with paced Playwright navigation instead of reading the site's file list. The book is larger than the default --max-pages bound, so re-run with --skip-existing until it reports no new pages (about 2000 topics).

purpose: AOS-CX per-switch-platform feature/release support matrix and AOS10 (AP/gateway) feature/release matrix, for RAG answers about hardware/software feature support.
notes: The page itself (https://feature-navigator.arubanetworking.hpe.com/wired and /aos10) is a client-rendered Next.js app with no data in its initial HTML, but its compiled JS bundles call a small unauthenticated public JSON API that returns the real comparison data directly: /api/productInfo lists every AOS-CX switch platform with its supported release list, /api/switchReleaseCompatibility?productId=&productReleaseNames=&licenses=1,2,3 returns that platform's full feature Yes/No matrix for the requested releases, and /api/releases + /api/releaseCompatibility?ids=&releases= do the same for the shared AOS10 (AP/gateway/Mobility Controller) image. Every published AOS-CX release is captured in a compact per-platform history JSON for exact comparisons; the latest snapshot is also rendered as Markdown for semantic search. The AOS10 side keeps every published release. 5 of the 25 productInfo entries (5400R, 3810, 2930F/M, 2540, 2530) are legacy ProVision/AOS-S platforms whose supportedReleases use AOS-S version strings (e.g. YA/YB.16.08.0001), not real AOS-CX releases, so they are deliberately skipped rather than queried; CX 4100i's supportedReleases also contains a literal "#REF!" Excel artifact that is filtered out.

purpose: Authoritative OpenAPI specs for exact endpoint, schema, field, and enum lookup.
notes: JSON specs are parsed into docs chunks and data/specs.sqlite; include CNAC via ingestion/scrape_cnac_spec.py and the pinned official Mist snapshot via ingestion/fetch_mist_openapi.py. ingestion/fetch_manifest_specs.py fetches the 30 registries named in openapi_registry_manifest.json by id. Coverage against the portal was then checked end to end: enumerating the new-central and new-central-config api-next sidebars yields 32 specs holding 2725 operations, of which 2713 were already on disk under registry-suffixed names, so ingestion/fetch_central_apinext_specs.py adds only wholly-new specs and reports the rest as drift. The portal no longer serves the per-slug specs (aaa-profile.json and friends) that the committed Central manifest was built from; both scrape_openapi.py and the api-next sidebar now return consolidated per-area documents, so those 243 files cannot be re-fetched.

purpose: AOS 10 techdocs books for Wi-Fi design, location services, private 5G, and AOS operations.
notes: Discover URLs with ingestion/discover_aos_urls.py and refresh with ingestion/scrape_aos_pw.py.

purpose: AOS-CX switch series release notes -- FULL history back to 10.13.xx (Overview, Enhancements, Resolved Issues, Feature Caveats, Known Issues, and 8 other sub-pages per patch) for all 14 published switch series.
notes: Distinct from aos_techdocs (AOS10 wireless/AP design guides) -- this is the switch OS's own release notes, previously an unaddressed gap. The consolidated portal's <select> dropdown maps each of the 14 switch series (4100i, 5420, 6000, 6100, 6200, 6300/6300L/6400, 8100, 8320, 8325, 8360, 8400, 9300, 9300S/10040, 10000) to a support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=... document holding that series' full multi-year patch history. The portal dropdown host (arubanetworks.com) returns HTTP 403 to plain TLS/headless clients (Akamai) and requires a non-headless Playwright browser with a realistic Chrome UA -- same constraint as aos_techdocs. support.hpe.com is NOT Akamai-fronted; it gates on a client-side anonymous-session JS check instead, a materially weaker/different mechanism that non-headless Playwright also satisfies. By explicit user decision (2026-08, superseding an earlier 'latest patch only' bound) this scrapes the FULL history back to the oldest available major-version group (currently AOS-CX 10.13.xx) and every patch within each group, not just the current release -- measured at ~10,400 pages total across all 14 series (roughly 800-930 pages per full-history series, 290-300 for the two newest/shortest-lived series). Output is laid out as <series-slug>/<patch-slug>/<page-slug>.html (patch is part of the path, not just the page slug, because the same ~13 page titles repeat once per patch). Discover with ingestion/discover_aoscx_release_notes_urls.py and refresh with ingestion/scrape_aoscx_release_notes.py; re-running later picks up any newly published patches/groups incrementally (existing on-disk files are skipped).

purpose: AOS-CX switch series Fundamentals and CLI Reference guides -- per-switch-series admin/config books and full CLI command reference, distinct from the release-notes changelog.
notes: Same support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=... viewer and gating mechanics as aoscx_release_notes (Playwright required, not Akamai-fronted, short 1-2s jitter), but these are plain books with no patch-history dimension. The docId list in discover_aoscx_guides_urls.py was assembled from live-verified search citations (each confirmed with a direct Playwright load + page=GUID link count), not guessed, and is deliberately NOT exhaustive across every AOS-CX switch-series generation yet -- 2 Fundamentals Guides (4100i/6000/6100; 5420/6200) and 6 CLI Reference guides (6000/6100, 6200, 6300/6400, 8100/8360, 8400, 10000) confirmed at ~14,574 pages total. Known gaps: CLI Reference for 9300/10040/5420, and Fundamentals Guide for 6300/6400, 8100/8320/8325/8360/9300/10000, and 8400 -- add more (label -> (docId, guide_type)) entries to DOC_IDS as they are found; nothing else needs to change. CLI Reference guides are large (1,300-2,900 pages each, one page per command) because each command's syntax/examples/history render as separate docDisplay pages; a slug-collision guard (short URL-hash suffix on duplicate titles within one guide) avoids generic repeated subsection headings (e.g. 'Examples') overwriting each other. Output is laid out as <guide-slug>/<page-slug>.html. Discover with ingestion/discover_aoscx_guides_urls.py and refresh with ingestion/scrape_aoscx_guides.py.

purpose: ClearPass Policy Manager Online Help -- the standalone on-prem CPPM admin/config guide, distinct from Central's cloud-hosted NAC feature docs (nac_docs).
notes: nac_docs covers Aruba Central's own cloud-hosted NAC/MAC-registration/MPSK features, not standalone ClearPass Policy Manager (CPPM) -- this source fills that gap. Same support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=... viewer/gating as the AOS-CX guides (Playwright required, short 1-2s jitter). Scoped to the current 6.14 release only (docId sd00007218en_us, confirmed live at 1,243 pages) -- unlike release notes, a Policy Manager user guide is a cumulative 'how it works today' reference, not a per-version changelog, so older major versions (6.11, 6.12, ...) would mostly duplicate the same configuration guidance rather than add distinct historical content. Add an older docId only if a version-specific behavior question needs it. Output is laid out as <page-slug>.html with the same slug-collision guard as aoscx_guides. Discover with ingestion/discover_clearpass_guide_urls.py and refresh with ingestion/scrape_clearpass_guide.py.

purpose: Official HPE Aruba Networking CSAF security advisories across hardware, software, cloud, NAC, SD-WAN, and management products.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. The incremental changes.csv feed covers the complete official Aruba advisory archive and preserves advisory IDs, CVEs, severity, affected products, fixed versions, and remediation text.

purpose: Official HPE Networking end-of-sale, replacement-product, and support-lifecycle notices across all networking product categories.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. The XML feed is the data source behind HPE's historical all-product End of Sale archive (no current Aruba-branded entries; nothing published after 2020); the official hardware PDF adds SKU-level dates and replacements but is a static 2020-05-06 snapshot. HPE does not publish a current crawlable index for every individual modern notice, so answers must cite the notice date and avoid implying the archive is exhaustive beyond its published entries. See docs/source-lifecycle-coverage.md and ingestion.scrape_security_lifecycle.HPE_ARUBA_CURRENT_LIFECYCLE_COVERAGE_GAP for the full evidenced coverage-gap boundary for current Aruba-branded lifecycle notices.

purpose: Official Juniper lifecycle milestone tables for the Mist and Apstra product families exposed by hpe-networking-mcp's optional backends.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. Juniper publishes these as server-rendered lifecycle tables rather than a public structured feed. discover_juniper_lifecycle_urls() additionally re-derives this same reviewed set (and any future officially-added Mist/Apstra page) from the official EOL index nav at the last seed_urls entry, deduplicated by absolute URL.

purpose: Official Juniper security bulletins for the Mist and Apstra product families exposed by hpe-networking-mcp's optional backends.
notes: Refresh with ingestion/scrape_security_lifecycle.py. discover_juniper_security_sitemaps() fetches and parses the official sitemap index above into its current topic-article child sitemap URLs (host/scheme/path validated, sitemap-topicarticle-*.xml only); discover_juniper_security_urls() then reads each child sitemap and filters to Mist/Apstra Security Bulletin articles. Playwright renders the Salesforce article body because plain HTTP receives only the application shell.

purpose: Juniper support-portal knowledge articles for Mist and Apstra: troubleshooting, licensing, and configuration guidance.
notes: Covers the Mist/Apstra articles that scrape_security_lifecycle.py leaves behind: it keeps only the formal Security Bulletins, which are a tiny fraction of the in-scope articles. The portal is a Salesforce Lightning app whose raw HTML holds no article text, so pages must be rendered with Playwright (headless=False).

purpose: Juniper Mist-family documentation (wireless, wired, WAN, access assurance, Juniper Validated Designs, and the Mist/Marvis-based data center + routing assurance products) for fuzzy howto/concept RAG search.
notes: URLs discovered from juniper.net's public sitemap (discover_mist_docs_urls.py matches 5 path prefixes: mist, jvd, hpe-mist-networking-data-center-assurance, juniper-data-center-assurance, juniper-routing-assurance — all Mist/Marvis-family products; excludes Junos core-OS and unrelated Juniper product lines as out of scope), then scraped via plain urllib + pandoc (server-rendered DITA HTML, no Playwright needed) with a 4-worker pool and a 0.4s per-request delay to avoid rate-limiting/IP bans. 2,014 URLs scraped as of the last full run (2,011 OK, 3 stale sitemap 404s). Excludes /software/mist/api/ (JS widget) — see mist_openapi_spec in openapi_specs' extra_scripts for the real API spec.

purpose: Complete official Junos CLI reference pages, including configuration statements, operational commands, syntax, hierarchy, and release information.
notes: discover_junos_cli_urls.py parses Juniper's official __toc.js into the current complete page inventory (about 11,700 pages). scrape_junos_cli.py fetches server-rendered .topicBody content with a bounded worker pool, extracts #topic-content, converts it to Markdown with Pandoc, preserves source URLs, and supports --skip-existing for resumable refreshes. The generated source directory is git-ignored.

purpose: Complete Juniper Mist HTTP API reference prose, endpoint descriptions, authentication guidance, examples, models, enums, webhook events, and walkthroughs.
notes: The public API route is an APIMatic shell. discover_mist_api_docs.py resolves portal.js to the canonical generated JSON asset, validates its Sections document, and records the asset URL. scrape_mist_api_docs.py downloads that asset once and renders all 506 virtual $h/ pages, including nested endpoint/model/reference content, into stable Markdown files. The generated source directory is git-ignored; the canonical asset URL is retained in each file for freshness/provenance.

purpose: Juniper Mist cloud platform release notes ('Product Updates') -- one page per dated release since 2017, covering Marvis, Access/Wireless/Wired/WAN Assurance, Location Services, and Premium Analytics feature changes. This is the Mist-cloud-platform counterpart to aoscx_release_notes (switch OS release notes) -- distinct from mist_docs (evergreen howto/concept docs).
notes: This section is not in juniper.net's normal sitemap (mist_docs' discovery does not find it); instead the site ships a client-side TOC data file at product-updates/__toc.js (a JS variable, trivially convertible to JSON) listing every dated release page. By explicit user decision this keeps the FULL history (186 pages, July 2017 - present) rather than only recent releases, and excludes the parallel 'govcloud' release track (a separate, smaller set of GovCloud-only dated pages, out of scope for general design guidance). Two export templates exist across the 9-year span: pages from roughly 2025 onward are Confluence-exported (div.confluence-cont, with a leading in-page TOC stripped since it is link text, not prose); older pages have no dedicated content wrapper, so the scraper falls back to the whole <body> (minus script/style/survey-widget chrome), confirmed clean via direct sampling. Plain urllib works for both eras (no Akamai/bot gate on this host, unlike the AOS-CX docDisplay path), so this uses a 4-worker pool with a 0.4s per-request delay, same pattern as scrape_mist_docs.py -- no Playwright needed.

purpose: Juniper EX-series switch hardware install/maintenance guide -- site guidelines, cabling, power, safety, chassis component replacement, and first-boot 'configure Junos OS' pages, per EX chassis family.
notes: Found via the same juniper.net sitemap crawl as mist_docs (plain urllib, no Playwright/bot-gate) filtered to /documentation/us/en/hardware/ex* paths -- confirmed 720 pages across every EX chassis family (ex2300, ex3400, ex4000, ex4100(-f/-h), ex4300, ex4400, ex4600, ex4650, ex9204/9208/9214/9251/9253). Same DITA topicBody template as mist_docs, confirmed via direct sampling, so ingestion/scrape_junos_docs.py reuses that extraction logic verbatim. This is predominantly a physical install/maintenance book (413 'concept' pages, mostly site/cabling/power/safety, plus 268 topic-map index pages); only ~14 pages are first-boot 'configure Junos OS' content -- deeper feature/CLI configuration guidance lives in the general Junos software config guides, a much larger (~24,700-page) corpus already deliberately excluded (see the same note on mist_docs' discovery script). Discover and scrape both junos_ex_hardware and junos_ex_release_notes together with ingestion/discover_junos_urls.py (pre-phase) and ingestion/scrape_junos_docs.py -- one script pair now produces/consumes all eight EX/MX/QFX/SRX hardware+release-notes datasets since they share the same sitemap crawl and scrape mechanics (formerly discover_junos_ex_urls.py/scrape_junos_ex.py, EX-only; generalized in place -- see junos_mx_hardware/junos_qfx_hardware/junos_srx_hardware notes for the MX/QFX/SRX expansion).

purpose: Juniper Junos OS release notes filtered to EX-series-specific pages -- per-version new features, resolved issues, open issues, and what-changed content for the EX platform only.
notes: The full Junos release-notes tree is 6,627 pages covering EVERY Junos platform (ACX/EX/MX/NFX/PTX/QFX/SRX/SSR/JRR/vSRX/cSRX), not just switches -- by the same 'bound to this project's switch/AP focus' reasoning already applied to aoscx_release_notes and mist_product_updates, only the 193 pages whose filename carries an explicit 'ex-' platform tag (e.g. ex-new-features-cover.html, ex-open-issues-23.1r1.html, ex-what-changed-22.3r2.html) are kept. MX/QFX/SRX now have their own equivalent sources (see junos_mx_release_notes/junos_qfx_release_notes/junos_srx_release_notes); still deliberately excluded: ACX/NFX/PTX/SSR/JRR-tagged pages (out of this project's router/switch/AP/firewall scope) and ~3,224 platform-generic feature pages (e.g. software-installation-and-upgrade, jweb, system-management, evpn, pki -- may or may not apply to any one platform, not filterable by filename alone, a candidate for later reconsideration if cross-platform feature content becomes valuable). Same sitemap-crawl/topicBody mechanics as junos_ex_hardware -- both datasets are produced by one run of ingestion/discover_junos_urls.py and scraped by one run of ingestion/scrape_junos_docs.py.

notes: Same 6,627-page full Junos release-notes tree as junos_ex_release_notes, filtered instead to pages whose filename carries an explicit 'mx-' platform tag (e.g. mx-new-features-cover.html, mx-open-issues-23.1r1.html, mx-what-changed-22.3r2.html). purpose: OpenAPI specs for the non-Central Aruba developer-portal products: AOS-CX, AOS-8, Central 2.x, ClearPass, UXI, Fabric Composer, and EdgeConnect Orchestrator.
notes: These seven portal sections run ReadMe's api-next v2 API, so they carry no oasPublicUrl pointer for scrape_openapi.py to parse, and the admin /apis listing is 403 for anonymous callers. The public per-page reference endpoint embeds the whole OpenAPI document under data.api.schema, so one fetch per sidebar category recovers every spec. Kept separate from openapi_specs (Central-only) so the generated Central client and manifest are unaffected; these are embedded for semantic search rather than added to the exact SQLite spec index. Discovery manifest: ingestion/product_specs_manifest.json.

purpose: Official Juniper EX-series switch and Mist-family access-point hardware datasheet specifications (port density, throughput, PoE, Wi-Fi standard, radios, mounting) for exact hardware-spec RAG lookup.
notes: URLs are filtered directly out of juniper.net's flat product sitemap (2,130 <loc> entries; distinct from the documentation sitemap discover_mist_docs_urls.py reads) rather than cached to a seed file, because the whole corpus is ~50 pages fetched in well under a minute — not the multi-hour crawl that justifies mist_docs_urls.json. EX-series .../specs.html pages extract div.cmp-specifications (a stable Adobe Experience Manager component verified across EX2300-EX9250); AP .../*-datasheet.html pages have no such wrapper but always carry exactly 5 <table> elements with the real spec content, rendered generically (a table whose first row has >2 cells becomes a markdown comparison table, otherwise label/value bullets). Aruba/HPE-branded hardware pages (arubanetworks.com, arubanetworking.hpe.com, www.hpe.com) were probed from this environment and every one returned an Akamai 403 or a hard HTTP/2 stream reset — including via a genuine headless-Chromium Playwright request — so this source is Juniper-only by evidenced necessity, not by choice; Aruba CX/AP exact specs are served instead by hpe_networking_mcp.pipeline.clients.hardware_specs, which ask_docs consults before RAG.
